title: Choose stackup and reference layers before routing
summary: Select layer roles around signal reference paths and routing needs. Establish edge rates, sensitive nets and manufacturing capabilities before choosing a stackup.
applies_to: Multilayer boards carrying fast digital or sensitive analog signals.
required_inputs: Per-layer copper and dielectric thicknesses, not only finished board thickness
verification: Read back board stackup and net rules; inspect each critical route's reference layer.
limitations: Example stackups are conditional. Layer count alone does not establish signal integrity. Compare ground-reference and power-distribution tradeoffs explicitly.

title: Preserve signal return paths across reference planes
summary: Avoid routing fast signals across reference-plane gaps. A return-current detour increases loop area; inspect the copper beneath the entire route.
applies_to: Signals relying on a nearby plane for high-frequency return current.
verification: Refill zones, then inspect crossings and reference continuity along the route.
limitations: A ground net name or successful DRC does not prove a continuous return path. Isolation boundaries require separate design review.

title: Minimize the decoupling capacitor connection loop
summary: Give local decoupling a short, low-inductance connection to the IC supply and ground. Inspect the return connection as well as capacitor proximity.
applies_to: IC supply bypassing, including analog and mixed-signal devices.
required_inputs: Supply/ground pin and capacitor pad locations
verification: Inspect the complete IC power pin-capacitor-ground return path and its vias; a nearby capacitor body alone is insufficient.
limitations: Capacitor values and acceptable inductance depend on the device and power network; this guide supplies no universal distance or capacitance.

citations.locator: Low and High Frequency Decoupling, pages 3-4, Figure 2

title: Choose mixed-signal grounding from current paths
summary: Keep digital switching currents from corrupting analog references. Ground-pin names alone do not determine whether system planes should be split.
applies_to: Mixed-signal converters and associated analog/digital circuitry.
required_inputs: Digital current levels and system interconnects
verification: Review ground topology and shared return impedances against the device documentation.
limitations: Converter architectures differ. Flag conflicting sources; do not join isolated grounds or impose one grounding topology automatically.

citations.locator: Grounding and Decoupling Mixed-Signal ICs, pages 6-8; high digital currents, page 13

title: Calculate trace width and pair gap from the fabrication stackup
summary: Derive controlled-impedance geometry from the selected fabrication stackup, routing layer, copper and target impedance. Coupled traces also require spacing inputs.
applies_to: Single-ended or differential routes with a specified impedance target.
verification: Use a suitable impedance calculator or field solver; record assumptions and read back the chosen net-class dimensions.
limitations: The cited calculator has manufacturing-specific restrictions. A copied width does not establish impedance on another stackup. This is not a current-capacity calculation.

citations.locator: Calculator inputs, supported structures and restrictions

title: Keep differential geometry and timing within interface requirements
summary: Route pair members with consistent geometry and reference conditions. Apply the selected interface's impedance and skew requirements; limit asymmetric breakouts.
applies_to: High-speed differential interfaces within the cited guide's scope.
required_inputs: Pair identities, stackup and skew budget
verification: Inspect pair paths, gaps and transitions; compare measured geometry against explicit constraints.
limitations: Equal copper lengths alone do not prove equal delay or interface compliance. Numeric limits vary by interface.

title: Account for return paths and stubs at signal vias
summary: When changing between ground references, connect those ground planes near the signal transition. For a ground-to-power reference change, review an appropriate AC return path instead. Review via stubs and pair symmetry.
applies_to: High-speed routes using vias or changing reference layers.
verification: Inspect transitions and nearby reference connections; assess stubs using fabrication data and channel analysis where needed.
limitations: A nearby ground via helps only when it connects the relevant ground references. No universal stitching pitch or back-drilling requirement is supplied.

title: Place connector protection around the discharge path
summary: Locate suitable transient protection near external signal entry points and give its return connection low inductance. Consider the path taken by discharge current.
applies_to: Externally accessible interfaces requiring transient protection.
verification: Inspect connector-protection-return routing and validate the assembled system under its required immunity tests.
limitations: A component ESD rating or clean DRC does not establish system immunity. Protection selection is interface-specific.

title: Keep crystal and load components close to oscillator pins
summary: Place the crystal circuit close to the device oscillator pins, with nearby load components and short connections. Keep unrelated routing away from the oscillator region.
applies_to: MCU crystal oscillator layouts; consult the selected device's recommendations.
verification: Inspect crystal connections and nearby routing; verify startup and clock performance on hardware.
limitations: Guarding, ground beneath the crystal and load capacitance depend on the oscillator design. Source dimensions are not universal placement constraints.

title: Group circuitry by function and separate interference paths
summary: Arrange related circuitry together and consider how noise travels between functional regions. Placement should support the intended signal and return-current paths.
applies_to: Boards mixing sensitive, switching and externally connected circuitry.
verification: Establish connector mating, mounting-hole and enclosure constraints before placing unconstrained functional circuitry.
Review placement and crossing routes against the functional diagram; document compromises.
limitations: Functional grouping is not a requirement to split ground planes. This is qualitative guidance, not an automatic placement algorithm. Mechanical-first ordering is an editorial workflow; positions and clearances come from the actual assembly drawings.

citations.locator: Section 3.1, Board structure - functional grouping, page 14

title: Choose impedance requirements; do not default every trace to 50 ohms
summary: Determine whether controlled impedance is required from the interface/device requirements and the signal edge rate relative to route propagation delay. A 50-ohm target is not universal and is not a termination resistor to add automatically.
applies_to: Signal-integrity planning before choosing net constraints, trace dimensions or termination.
required_inputs: Interface generation, driver/receiver requirements and topology
Driver rise/fall times, route propagation delay and actual stackup
Specified single-ended or differential target and tolerance, if applicable
verification: Distinguish characteristic impedance from DC copper resistance and single-ended from differential impedance.
Use a suitable model and fabrication stackup to derive geometry; evaluate termination with driver impedance and receiver timing.
Check receiver waveforms for ringing and valid transitions; DRC cannot establish signal integrity.
limitations: Short GPIO/UART/I2C links have no blanket 50-ohm requirement; fast edges can still require transmission-line analysis. Power paths need current, voltage-drop and transient-impedance review, not a 50-ohm target. Do not infer width from impedance without stackup data.

citations.locator: Sections 1.2-1.3 and 2.4: edge rates, transmission lines and termination
